data.narrative:
Copenhagen Atomics is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $25M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 companies across the nuclear sector—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Valar Atomics, Fuse Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, and X-Energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $25M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $50M. Peer-median analysis identifies three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations of $6.0B (Valar Atomics, Series B), $808M (Nano Nuclear Energy, Seed), and $200M (Fuse Energy, Series A), producing a median of $808M. The peer range spans $200M to $6.0B, reflecting substantial heterogeneity in the nuclear landscape.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $42M to $929M, with a median of $429M. The wide spread reflects two distinct methodologies: stage-progression anchors to observable capital deployed, while peer-median captures market pricing of comparable-stage nuclear ventures but is sensitive to the early-stage, high-risk profile of the sample. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to the peer set, capital intensity of the development path, and regulatory pathway clarity. A Series A valuation in the $100M–$300M range would position Copenhagen Atomics between pure stage progression and the lower quartile of peer valuations.
